text: UN General Assembly resolutions are not binding sources of international law under Article 38 of the ICJ Statute; under the UN Charter (Arts. 10 and 13) they are recommendations. Their legal weight is indirect: they can be evidence of customary international law where they reflect widespread state practice and *opinio juris*, as the ICJ found in *Nicaragua* (1986), and some are binding only within the UN system, such as budget decisions.
